why: [R-GAP-03] with the ratchet of [R-ENF-02]. Every published name more than ten per cent from its own published spot on the day the rule was adopted (07-09-2026) and carrying no CURRENT audit of the number the site actually shows. Each entry carries its MEASURED gap. The build breaks on a NEW breach with no current audit, or on a published name whose answer becomes unreadable. This list may only ever get SHORTER (--prune). IT SPLITS INTO TWO KINDS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME DEBT: names with no study directory, which nothing could audit; and names WITH a study and a review, where the review audits the study's rebuilt answer and the site still carries the pre-rebuild one, because [R-GAP-02] holds the book from publishing. The second kind is not a review going stale — it is a PAGE going stale, and it is the more serious of the two. [R-ENF-08, 07-09-2026]: each entry now carries the MAGNITUDE it excuses. A ratchet entry is a ticker, so before this a listed name was excused from the whole gate — the injection harness planted SABIC at 40% of its spot and nothing fired, because SABIC was already listed at +10.8%. An entry excuses a deviation up to the size it records, plus the same five-point tolerance [R-GAP-01 AMENDED] uses for a stale audited gap; a materially worse breach on a listed name is a NEW breach.
